How it works

  1. Pick a calculator and choose metric (kg, cm) or imperial (lb, feet, inches).
  2. Enter your numbers. Friendly messages tell you if something looks wrong.
  3. Read your estimate and the explanation of what it can and cannot tell you.

Learn before you measure

Short, plain-English guides on what the numbers mean and where they fall short.

What BMI can and cannot tell you

A plain-English guide to adult BMI: how it is calculated, what the categories mean, and why it should never be the only measure of health.

Waist-to-height ratio explained

How to measure your waist correctly, how to calculate waist-to-height ratio, what the 0.5 guideline means, and when the measure is not suitable.

How much protein do you need?

Understand protein reference values per kilogram of body weight, why activity changes the picture, and why more protein is not automatically better.

Tracking measurements consistently

Practical tips for measuring weight, waist, hips and chest in a consistent way, reading trends calmly, and keeping your records safe.

Privacy first

Calculations run in your browser. There are no accounts, and your measurements are not sent to a server. The Measurement Tracker saves records only in your browser's localStorage. Read the privacy policy.

What these tools cannot do

These tools give general estimates for adults. They do not diagnose conditions, prescribe diets or treatments, or promise results. No weight is right for everyone. See the medical disclaimer and speak with a qualified healthcare professional about your health.

Frequently asked questions

Are the calculators free?

Yes. They need no registration.

Is my data stored or shared?

Calculators keep nothing. The tracker stores records in your own browser only, and nothing is uploaded.

Is this medical advice?

No. It is educational information. Consult a qualified healthcare professional for medical advice.

Can I use metric or imperial units?

Yes. Every tool supports kilograms and centimetres, or pounds, feet and inches.
